title: GPT-5.2 Derives & Proves Nonzero Single-Minus Gluon Scattering Amplitudes
whyItMatters: Overturned a decades-old textbook assumption in Yang–Mills theory by conjecturing and proving an exact closed-form formula for nonzero single-minus n-gluon tree amplitudes.
summary: Collaborating with physicists from the Institute for Advanced Study, Harvard, and Cambridge, an internal scaffolded GPT-5.2 model reasoned for ~12 hours to conjecture a piecewise-constant closed-form formula for tree-level n-gluon scattering with one negative-helicity gluon in half-collinear (Klein-space / complexified) kinematics—previously assumed to vanish—and produced a formal proof verified via Berends–Giele recursion and Weinberg’s soft theorem. Within weeks, the team extended the result to gravitons.
technicalHighlights: Conjectured an all-n closed-form expression for single-minus tree-level gluon amplitudes and proved it via Berends–Giele recursion.
Verified consistency with Weinberg’s soft theorem and generalized within a month to single-minus graviton amplitudes (arXiv:2603.04330).
Co-authored with leading theoretical physicists including Andrew Strominger and David Skinner.
caveats: Applies to special half-collinear complexified/Klein-space kinematics rather than generic real Minkowski momenta, and prompt/scaffolding logs were not fully released.

scoreRationale.foundational: Corrected a widely taught vanishing assumption in tree-level Yang–Mills amplitude theory and yielded an all-n formula.
scoreRationale.ripple: Immediately extended to graviton scattering amplitudes and sparked a wave of AI-assisted theoretical physics.
scoreRationale.verification: Analytically verified against Berends–Giele recursion and Weinberg soft limits by leading QFT physicists; awaiting journal publication.
scoreRationale.velocity: Synthesized a clean all-n formula and proof in ~12 hours of scaffolded reasoning.
